body:
m1 red-team of the key-lifetime seam (answering msg-01M15FHZZ0V0F90H4XSFPYF59D; chief to ratify or amend).

Principle: key authority is BATCH-scoped and captured exactly once. A batch has one KeyId K from its snapshot, taken before any non-public delegation; every receipt, digest and amendment that escapes the batch is under K. Nothing under any other key is ever carried, and no path returns a receipt that is not under K. That gives one law to test: for every batch exactly one AttemptReceipt escapes; its digest authority is Keyed(K) (or Plain for an all-public batch, or Withheld(K) when call-free); its call list equals the ProviderCalls actually made. Call it the "always under K" law.

Case 1 - the returned keyed receipt names K' != K. That is not rotation, it is a contract violation by the delegate (or a laundering attempt: digests under an unverifiable key). Typed outcome: EmbedError.ReceiptKeyMismatch(expected: KeyId, found: KeyId) -> the batch is BatchRejected. Provenance is NOT dropped: the escaping receipt is minted fresh under K with calls = the ProviderCall list as made (call identity carries provider fingerprint, counts, timing, request params - no material, so it is safe under any key), receipts = empty, and a typed ResultDecision.ReceiptRejected(ReceiptKeyMismatch(K, K')) plus every item outcome Invalid(ReceiptKeyMismatch). The foreign receipt BODY (its item/outputs digests) is what gets dropped, because digests under K' cannot be verified or compared under K and may be Plain in disguise. KeyId is an identifier, never derived from key bytes, so naming K' in the decision is not a leak. This is the same shape I recommended for the cache Left path (fresh keyed call-free rejection), extended with call provenance when calls were made.

Case 2 - amendment fails after provider work. Make it nearly unrepresentable: addResultDecisions takes the batch's SensitiveKeySnapshot (immutable, copied bytes, held by the batch for its whole duration - CachingEmbedder already has it), not a provider. Then re-capture cannot fail for key withdrawal; the only failure left is snapshot.keyId != receipt.digest.keyId, i.e. a programming error, surfaced as Left(EmbedError.AuthorityMismatch(stored, supplied)). The caller (CachingEmbedder / conforming) converts that Left exactly as in case 1: fresh rejection receipt under K with the calls made and all outcomes Invalid. An unamended receipt never escapes; a provider-sourced re-capture never exists. Key withdrawal between batches is then the ONLY withdrawal case, and it is already the keyless fail-closed Withheld path before delegation.

Case 3 - Embedder.conforming with no key for a non-public batch: fail closed before delegation (Withheld(K) is impossible without K, so this is EmbedError.NoKey with the requested KeyId if the policy names one; the deferred low from P0-2) and mint the call-free Withheld receipt only when a KeyId is known; otherwise the batch result is Left and no receipt claims authority it does not have.

What I would reject: (a) carrying the delegate's receipt "for audit" - an unverifiable body is not an audit trail, the call list is; (b) any amendment API that accepts a provider (re-capture) rather than the snapshot; (c) a receipt kind that mixes authorities (items under K, outputs under K') - the whole-value v2 digest must be under one KeyId, and validateProviderReceipts should assert it. Tests to pin: a delegate returning K' yields Left-derived rejection under K with calls preserved and zero foreign digests anywhere in the escaping receipt (grep the rendering for K'-keyed lines); withdrawing the key mid-batch (provider returns None after snapshot) changes nothing in the batch's receipt; snapshot/keyId mismatch at amendment is a typed Left and the escaping receipt is still under K; conforming without a key makes no delegate call (call counter stays 0).
